security_audit.summary: This is a benign documentation skill from the official anthropics plugin repository that teaches how to author Claude Code agents (frontmatter, triggering descriptions, system prompts). All 82 static findings were adjudicated as false positives: the external_commands hits are Markdown code fences, inline-code spans, and file:line references in prose; the two path-traversal hits are JSON example strings containing escaped newlines and no traversal; the blocker hits are ordinary documentation bullets. The single shell script is a read-only YAML frontmatter validator with no command-injection vector. No prompt injection, data-exfiltration intent, or malicious behavior was found.

remediation.issue: scripts/validate-agent.sh interpolates a user-supplied file path into shell command substitutions without validation.
remediation.suggestion: The script is read-only and low risk, but for robustness quote and validate the path argument and prefer passing filenames to tools directly rather than through unquoted expansions; consider rejecting paths that are not regular readable files before processing.

content.value_statement: Writing Claude Code subagents by hand is error-prone because the frontmatter, triggering descriptions, and system prompts must follow exact conventions. This skill gives you templates, examples, and a validator so your agents are structured correctly and trigger reliably.
actual_capabilities: Explains the required agent file format with YAML frontmatter and a Markdown system prompt body.
Documents every frontmatter field (name, description, model, color, tools) and its allowed values.
Provides complete, copy-ready agent examples for review, testing, documentation, and security use cases.
Shows how to write triggering descriptions with example blocks so agents activate on the right requests.
Includes a shell script that validates agent files for correct structure and field constraints.
Covers agent organization, namespacing, and testing workflows for Claude Code plugins.
limitations: It teaches agent authoring for Claude Code plugins only; it does not create or run agents by itself.
The validator is a Bash script and requires a Unix-like shell to run.
Guidance reflects the agent format conventions at the time of writing and may lag later format changes.
It does not test whether an agent actually triggers inside a live Claude Code session.

use_cases.title: Author a new review agent
use_cases.description: A plugin developer follows the templates to write a code-review agent with correct frontmatter and a structured system prompt.

use_cases.title: Standardize a team's agents
use_cases.description: A tech lead uses the field reference and validator to enforce consistent naming, tools, and prompt structure across many agents.

use_cases.title: Learn agent triggering
use_cases.description: A newcomer studies the example blocks to understand how description text controls when an agent activates.
use_cases.target_user: Developer new to Claude Code agents

prompt_templates.title: Create a basic agent
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an agent that reviews code for quality issues. Give it correct frontmatter and a clear system prompt.

prompt_templates.title: Write a triggering description
prompt_templates.prompt: Write a description field with two example blocks so this agent triggers when a user asks to generate unit tests.

prompt_templates.title: Restrict agent tools
prompt_templates.prompt: Update my analysis agent to use only read-only tools following the principle of least privilege.

prompt_templates.title: Design a full security agent
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a security analysis agent with a complete system prompt, structured output format, edge-case handling, and validate it against the agent file rules.

output_examples.input: Create an agent that reviews code for quality issues.
output_examples.output: A ready-to-save agent file with a name, a description containing example blocks, model set to inherit, a color, and a structured system prompt listing responsibilities, process steps, and output format.

output_examples.input: Write a description field so this agent triggers on test-generation requests.
output_examples.output: A description that opens with the triggering conditions and includes example blocks showing the user request, the assistant response, and commentary explaining why the agent activates.

best_practices: Include two to four concrete example blocks in the description so the agent triggers on the right requests.
Restrict the tools field to the minimum the agent needs, following the principle of least privilege.
Write the system prompt in second person with clear responsibilities, process steps, and a defined output format.
anti_patterns: Writing a vague, generic description with no example blocks, which makes triggering unreliable.
Granting an agent access to all tools when it only needs to read files.
Writing the system prompt in first person or leaving the output format undefined.

faq.question: What is a Claude Code agent?
faq.answer: An agent is an autonomous subprocess that handles complex, multi-step tasks. It is defined in a Markdown file with YAML frontmatter and a system prompt body.

faq.question: What fields does an agent file require?
faq.answer: The required fields are name, description, model, and color. The tools field is optional and restricts which tools the agent may use.

faq.question: How does an agent know when to activate?
faq.answer: The description field defines the triggering conditions. It should include example blocks showing the user request and the assistant response so the agent activates on matching intent.

faq.question: Which model value should I choose?
faq.answer: Use inherit so the agent uses the same model as the parent, unless the agent needs a specific model. Other options are sonnet, opus, and haiku.

faq.question: How do I limit what an agent can do?
faq.answer: Set the tools field to an array of only the tools the agent needs. For read-only analysis, list only reading and search tools.

faq.question: How do I check that an agent file is valid?
faq.answer: Run the included validate-agent.sh script on the agent file. It checks the frontmatter structure, required fields, and field formats.
